title: Connection State View
description: Payload of the view:connection_state bridge message — the Transport Client's connection_status, serialized across the CEF bridge so the UI can show whether the extension is talking to the server (Requirement 3.4). No envelope carries this: the connection's own state cannot arrive over the connection, which is the clearest case in the bridge contract for a view model rather than a forwarded payload. Produced on the network thread, handed to the main thread through the queue pair, and published from the tick — never written to CEF directly (Requirements 2.3, 22.2).

state.description: The three states requirement 3.4 names. reconnecting covers both the backoff wait and an attempt in flight: from the producer's side they are the same condition, and distinguishing them would invite a UI that flickers between two labels.

consecutiveFailedAttempts.description: Failures since the last successful connection, reset to zero by a success. The UI can use it to stop showing a transient blip as an outage.

reconnectionDelayMilliseconds.description: The delay currently being waited out, from requirement 3.2's schedule — 500 ms doubling per consecutive failure, capped at 30 seconds. Zero when nothing is scheduled. Milliseconds are named in the field rather than left to a comment, because the C++ member is a std::chrono::milliseconds and a bare number crossing a bridge into TypeScript has no unit at all.

requiredProducerAction.description: Whether the producer has to do something before the extension can reconnect. none means connected, or reconnecting on its own. close_the_other_reaper_instance is requirement 3.5's duplicate-client-type case, which never retries. sign_in_again is requirement 3.6's, where the token could not be renewed. This is the field the UI should branch and translate on.

notice.description: Producer-facing English, authored in C++. The UI should render a translation selected by state and requiredProducerAction and treat this as a fallback — react-i18next covers seven locales and the extension's C++ has no translation catalogue, so a UI that displayed this verbatim would be English-only for exactly the messages a producer reads when something is wrong (Requirement 15.3).

lastRejection.description: Why the last handshake was refused, classified. Absent when no handshake has been refused since the last successful connection. For diagnosis rather than display: requiredProducerAction already says what the producer can do about it, and unrecognised means the server's protocol is ahead of this build.

$comment: There is no field here for a token, an expiry, or any part of one, and additionalProperties false is what keeps it that way: requirement 26.1 puts token material in memory only, and the CEF renderer is a separate process running agent-authored markdown. The Catch2 suite already asserts the C++ struct carries none; this is the same assertion one layer out.
